_comment: Lighthouse in CI, on the mobile profile (the default: throttled 4G, mid-range phone).
Audits the signed-out app: a static build has neither API nor Keycloak behind it, so
what is measured is the shell — boot, theme, fonts, first paint, the sign-in prompt.
That is the part every visitor pays for, and the only part measurable reproducibly;
the signed-in screens need the whole stack and belong to the e2e suite.
Home and Collection render the same sign-in prompt while signed out, but both are
kept so the check follows if they ever diverge.
Thresholds — measured, not wished for. See .claude/docs/CONVENTIONS.md § 4.
accessibility and best practices came back at 1.00 on every run, on CI and locally:
they carry no timing, so they cannot flap, and they are asserted just under.
performance cannot be asserted at the 0.9 the v1.0 milestone wants. Eighteen runs
over three CI runs of the same code scored anywhere between 0.48 and 0.98, because
index.html blocks its first paint on a third-party stylesheet (Google Fonts) whose
latency belongs to somebody else. Two decisions follow. The aggregation is the
median rather than LHCI's default optimistic pick, so one lucky run cannot hide a
regression and one unlucky run cannot invent one — the 0.48 above is exactly the
sample a median throws away. And the threshold is a floor at 0.5, 0.22 under the
lowest median CI has produced: it still fails a build that ships a genuinely heavy
regression, and it never goes red on the weather. It gets raised to 0.9 by the
change that takes the fonts off the critical path — a red check nobody can predict
teaches people to ignore red checks.
